products.name: Notion Q&A
products.note: Knowledge base AI Q&A; workspace corpus access; permission-aware but broad exposure risk

reading.body:
Notion embeds AI into its workspace platform rather than offering it as a standalone product, meaning its compute demands scale with workspace adoption and usage intensity rather than dedicated inference infrastructure.

The architecture matters for grid strain. Notion AI's features—chat, Q&A against user corpora, autonomous agents, and meeting transcription—all run on third-party LLM provider infrastructure via API, not Notion's own servers. This offloads raw compute to those providers' data centers. However, the permission-aware Q&A and custom agents that run on schedules or event triggers create a different load pattern than one-shot inference. Agents that execute repeatedly across connected apps like Slack and Google Drive can generate sustained API calls and persistent compute demand, even if individual requests are small. The credit-based pricing at $10 per 1,000 credits suggests Notion is metering and reselling API consumption, making it a demand aggregator rather than a compute owner.

The data does not reveal Notion's total inference volume, the latency requirements of its workspace integrations, or how many agents run concurrently across its user base. It also does not cover which LLM providers Notion uses or whether those providers are building dedicated capacity for Notion's traffic. For grid impact, what matters is whether Notion's growth translates to steady baseline load on provider infrastructure or bursty, hard-to-predict spikes. The data only confirms that the load exists and that it flows through external compute.

profile_text.body:
Notion Labs is a for-profit startup founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its site presents Notion as one tool that does it all, letting users search, generate, analyze, and chat inside Notion, and says AI agents handle repetitive tasks autonomously so teams do not have to. The company describes Notion AI as a built-in teammate that works directly in pages, docs, tasks, and databases, using context from the workspace and connected apps when enabled.

Notion AI is the company's general AI product, embedded in the workspace and knowledge base. The site lists Enterprise Search and Notion AI Connectors for searching across a workspace and connected apps such as Slack and Google Drive, and AI Meeting Notes for transcribing conversations and summarizing key points. Custom Agents can run on schedules or triggers and complete multi-step work across the workspace and connected tools. Notion AI is included with Business and Enterprise plans, with limited trial usage on other plans; Custom Agents run on Notion credits, sold as an add-on to those plans, priced at $10 per 1,000 credits after a free trial, with usage tracked in a credits dashboard. The company says access to AI features can be temporarily reduced depending on usage. It also says Notion AI supports HIPAA compliance through LLM providers' zero-retention APIs and can process protected health information, that customer data is not used to train models unless the customer opts in, and that data shared with AI subprocessors is covered by contracts prohibiting its use for training.

Notion Q&A is the company's knowledge base question-and-answer product, drawing on the workspace corpus; it is described as permission-aware, with broad exposure risk noted. Legal exposure recorded for the company is in California, with a count of 270.
